title: Isolation of Human Pancreatic Islets of Langerhans for Research
author: James Lyon
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bt55nq86

steps.title: Initial Setup and Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare all media, equipment, and the COBE system according to the specific Human Islet Isolation Media Preparation, Equipment Setup, and COBE Setup protocols.

steps.title: Organ Reception and Initial Handling
steps.instruction: Assign an internal identifying case number (sequential number preceded by 'R') to the received pancreas. Prepare the workspace and initial rinse solutions.

substeps.instruction: Pour 10% betadine into the first beaker.
Pour ~200 ml of HBSS into the second and third beakers.
Pour remaining HBSS into the cutdown tray.
Remove the pancreas/spleen/duodenum from the transport cooler, cutting closure ties down to the final sterile barrier.
Transfer the organ within the sterile barrier to the BSC dissection tray.
Remove the organ from the transport solution and pour 200-500 ml of the transport solution into the dissection tray.
Record the isolation start time.

steps.title: Pancreas Dissection and Decontamination
steps.instruction: Dissect the pancreas to expose the duct and perform surface decontamination.

substeps.instruction: Dissect away the spleen, major vessels (splenic artery/vein, mesenteric artery/vein), and excess fat.
Locate the bile duct and dissect it away from the pancreas toward the main drainage point at the duodenum.
Dissect the pancreas away from the duodenum toward the pancreatic duct.
Expose the pancreatic duct and cut through it close to the duodenum.
Place the trimmed pancreas in the 10% betadine beaker for ~1 minute.
Transfer the pancreas to the second beaker to rinse/agitate, then repeat with the third beaker.
Change sterile gloves and transfer the rinsed pancreas to the cutdown tray.

steps.title: Pancreas Cannulation
steps.instruction: Cannulate the pancreatic duct at the head, neck, and tail to allow for perfusion.

substeps.instruction: Insert a 16-gauge catheter into the exposed main pancreatic duct opening; secure with a bent internal needle and 3-0 silk suture (tying the wings of the cannula).
Inject HBSS via the cannula to locate the duct passage.
At the neck of the pancreas, use a scalpel to expose the main duct, dissect it bluntly, and isolate it with two 3-0 silks.
Cut a small hole in the exposed duct and insert a 16-gauge catheter toward the tail; tie off as done at the head.
Insert a final 16-gauge catheter toward the head and tie off as done at the head.

steps.title: Perfusion and Tissue Preparation
steps.instruction: Perform perfusion with a collagenase/protease solution and prepare the tissue for digestion.

substeps.instruction: Pat the pancreas dry with sterile 4x4 gauze and weigh it in a tared 500ml Nalgene container (record weight in grams).
Calculate the neutral protease dose based on cold ischemia time, organ consistency, and warm ischemia damage; add this to the prepared collagenase.
Pour the solution into the perfusion tray and prime the tubing at 100ml/min until air-bubble free.
Transfer the pancreas to the perfusion tray, clamp/plug the main duct opening, and attach perfusion channel 'A' to the head-directed cannula and channel 'B' to the tail-directed cannula.
Run the pre-programmed perfusion protocol, ensuring both head and tail sections distend; clamp any leaks.
Collect and record the collagenase solution volume and remove catheters.
Take a biopsy sample per the ex vivo protocol.
Cut the pancreas into 10-15 equal pieces, record any abnormalities and the consistency (soft, normal, fibrotic), and place pieces into a kidney bowl with silicon nitride marbles.

steps.title: Automated Digestion
steps.instruction: Digest the pancreatic tissue using the auto-isolator/Ricordi chamber system.

substeps.instruction: Drain the primed auto-isolator/Ricordi chamber by removing the inlet line and inverting the chamber.
Transfer pancreas pieces and marbles to the Ricordi chamber, install a 500µm stainless steel mesh, seal, and attach to the shaking arm.
Fill the digestion circuit with collagenase solution at 300mL/min.
Add DNase solution to a 250 mL conical containing collagenase and the Inlet 1/Outlet 1 rods; add perfusion/priming solution to remove all air.
Advance to step 4 (digest 1) and start timing. Once the system reaches 37 ± 1 °C (approx. 3-6 mins), advance to step 5 (digest 2).
Starting around the 8-10 minute mark, take 1ml samples every 2 minutes, stain with dithizone, and observe under a stereo-microscope for islet yield and quality.
Advance to step 6 (collection 1) once the lead tech determines the digest is complete.

steps.title: Tissue Collection and Initial Wash
steps.instruction: Collect the digested tissue and perform the first wash sequence.

substeps.instruction: Insert the intake rod into Dilution 2 solution and the outlet rod into the first of twelve 250 mL conical tubes containing 100ml of Dilution 1 (kept on a cold block); record the dilution time.
Collect digest into the twelve 100ml Dilution 1 tubes, followed by empty 250 mL tubes.
Centrifuge the first four full tubes at 282 x g, 4 °C, for 1 minute (1100 rpm).
Transfer pellets to a 1L bottle on ice containing ~200 mL Wash 1 media, disrupting pellets by gentle hand vortex.
After 2 L of Dilution 2 is added, invert the chamber (step 7), then allow air into the system for 30 seconds (step 8).
Continue collection/centrifugation/transfer until all 6 L of Dilution 2 is circulated.
Transfer the final suspension to four 250ml conical tubes and centrifuge at 282 x g, 4 °C, for 1 minute.
Transfer and disrupt pellets into one 250ml conical tube with Wash 1 media.
Sample 100 µL for dithizone staining to observe islet numbers, size, and % trapped.
Centrifuge the 250ml suspension at 282 x g, 4 °C, for 1 minute, remove supernatant, and weigh the pellet to the nearest 0.1g.

steps.title: Tissue Aliquoting
steps.instruction: Divide the tissue into aliquots for purification.

substeps.instruction: Divide the tissue into aliquots of no more than 30g using UW solution.
Add UW solution to each aliquot to reach a total volume of 150ml.
Store tubes on ice for at least 15 minutes.

steps.title: COBE Purification
steps.instruction: Purify the islets using the COBE 2991 system and density gradients.

substeps.instruction: Set COBE 2991: speed 1500 rpm, super out rate 0 mL/min, super out volume 600 mL.
Load 100 mL Biocoll (1.100 g/mL) into the cell processing bag using the gradient maker and Masterflex pump.
Press SUPER OUT, increase rate to 100 mL/min to fill tubing, then press STOP/RESET.
Set COBE speed to 3000 rpm and super out rate to 0 mL/min.
Load 'High' gradient into the front beaker, allow a few ml to flow to the rear beaker, then add 'Low' gradient to the rear beaker.
Turn on the stir plate and press START SPIN. Once at full speed, pump the gradient at 30ml/min until empty.
Pour UW/tissue suspension 50 ml at a time into the front beaker. Rinse the conical with 50ml Wash 1 and pour the rinse into the front beaker.
Clamp the main bag line above the metal seal, open the pump head, press SUPER OUT, and release haemostats.
Turn off the pump and time the purification for 5 minutes.
Place the collection rod in a conical tube containing 100 ml Wash solution 2; reconnect the COBE inlet line to the collection rod line.
Increase super out rate to 100 mL/min and collect tissue into twelve prefilled 250 mL conical tubes.
Centrifuge tubes at 280 x g, 4 °C, for 1 minute; record pellet volume and transfer/disrupt pellets into marked 50ml conical tubes using Wash 2.

steps.title: Purity Analysis and Layering
steps.instruction: Analyze the purity of the fractions and group them into layers.

substeps.instruction: Bring each 50ml tube to volume with Wash 2 and sample 100µl using a wide bore tip.
Transfer samples to a 24-well plate and stain with dithizone to designate purity layers: 'Top' (highest), 'Middle', and 'Bottom' (lowest).
Centrifuge designated tubes at 280 x g, 4 °C, for 1 minute and aspirate supernatant.
Combine pellets of the same layer into one 100 mL conical tube per layer using supplemented CMRL.
Record all data in the isolation batch record.

steps.title: Quality Control and Final Culture
steps.instruction: Perform final quality control sampling and transfer islets to culture dishes.

substeps.instruction: Perform sampling for Insulin, DNA, counts, and immunohistochemistry per the QC protocol.
Allow islets to gravity settle for at least 5 minutes.
Remove 5 mL of supernatant and incubate for 1 week at 37 °C (5% CO2) for contamination control; replace with culture media to maintain 100ml volume.
Transfer islet suspension to non-tissue culture treated 150mm x 15mm petri dishes (typically 40,000 to 60,000 islet equivalents per dish).
Add supplemented CMRL to reach a final volume of 35 mL per dish.
Incubate dishes at 22 °C (5% CO2) until distribution.
Record IEQ, purity, and % trapped in REDCap.
